items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: And, uh, so he hired me to play with him that night. Down at Rice, that's where I started with the guitar.

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah. Well, that's where Kenneas had it now. He was a violin player. He used to take cigarette, smoke cigarette and stick it behind his ear, you know, like that, and keep it lit, you see. And played violin. Nothing but soft music, you see. Yeah. Violin, guitar, bass, like that, you see. And, uh, so he hired me to play with him that night. Down at Rice, that's where I started with the guitar. And I think we made about 23 or 24 dollars a piece that night. I wasn't getting but nine dollars a week out to the…
You'd be quite young then, would you?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: And every night, well, I was working with him every night, he's a fellow, there's no one that's Canadian Jacks, he used to play the violin.

ctx.x: I want to ask... This is the second reel, the second side of Eddie Dawson? Yeah. I wanted to ask you if you had another kind of job for your, how you made your living, if you had a day job too. Or you just play music all the time. No, I didn't do no work. I didn't work at all. Didn't you work for a bank one time? That's after, long after. That's way back. You didn't work in a lumber yard or anything?

Yeah, before I went to the bank, I worked in a lumber yard, uh, Carrie's, uh, lumber yard, uh, on the basin, near the White Bridge there. You worked there a long time? Oh yeah, I worked there a long time. That's where I left from, to play music. Oh yeah? I was working in a lumber yard, in Cornelius Jackson, come back there and I was playing guitar then. This was a long time ago, this was... Yeah, I know, I was, uh, playing, uh, I used to play guitar. When I started, I started going around in the battlefield at…
A little cigarette. And you just played with him, he had two pieces, just guitar and violin. No, we had a bass, too.
